title: Specs Library Conventions
description: Facts about the libraries a spec was generated from and is generated for, keyed by platform. Every consumer reading the same libraries declares the same values; differing values produce incorrect output, not merely different output.

VariantStateEntry.description: Classifies a Figma variant prop as a semantic state concept. The map key (in specs.states) is the concept name (e.g. hover, disabled). (ADR-055, ADR-073)

value.description: Figma variant value that activates this concept (e.g. 'hover', 'pressed'). Omit for boolean props — defaults to 'true'.

contract.description: Overrides the concept's canonical browser-driven / consumer-controlled default.

PlatformConventions.description: Facts about one platform's library — how it is authored (encoding members) and what it calls things (vocabulary members). One permissive shape for every platform, including figma. Also the root of a single config/conventions/<platform>.yaml file, so one file validates standalone. (ADR-073, ADR-078)

naming.description: Naming convention this platform uses for layer and component property names — the reversal target for settings.spec.keys.

glyphs.description: Glyph content assets. Absence means the library has no glyph convention. A declared block carries at least one form — match, structure, or both; membership is the union.

match.description: Name form — membership and naming in one pattern over the component name, using the {i} icon-name placeholder.

codeOnlyProps.description: The code-only props container layer. Absence means the library has no such convention.

match.description: Literal layer name identifying the container.

subcomponents.description: Subcomponent organization and naming. Absence means the library has no subcomponent convention.

scope.description: Where the library keeps subcomponents. NESTED = anatomy only; PAGE = also the Figma page.

match.description: Naming patterns identifying subcomponents, using {C} and {S} placeholders.

exclude.description: Naming patterns for matched assets the library excludes.

instanceExamples.description: Instance example organization and naming (ADR-050). Absence means the library has no such convention.

scope.description: Where the library keeps instance examples.

match.description: Naming patterns narrowing which instance frames qualify, using the {C} placeholder.

exclude.description: Naming patterns for frames the library excludes.

parentNames.description: Immediate-parent frame or section names a candidate must sit within.

images.description: How this platform expresses images. Encoding: backgroundImage, sourceProps. Vocabulary: match (the Figma name of the designated image component) and component (the same component's name on this platform). Absence means no image convention. (ADR-063, ADR-077)

backgroundImage.description: Encoding. This platform expresses images as container fills, emitted as Styles.backgroundImage — always passed styling, never a primitive trigger. (ADR-077)

match.description: Vocabulary. Figma name of the designated image component (e.g. 'DS Image'). Requires a non-empty sourceProps.

sourceProps.description: Code-only prop names carrying image sources. The first entry is the designated component's own source prop.

component.description: Vocabulary. The same component's name on this platform (e.g. 'DsImage') — the translation target for a match declared by whichever platform produced the spec. Not validated against it; an unmatched component is inert. (ADR-077)

slotConstraints.description: The library authors slot constraints as code-only props, to be consolidated into the slot property.

inferNumberProps.description: The library authors numeric props as Figma TEXT props whose values parse as numbers, to be emitted as NumberProp.

stylesProp.description: Prop that receives styling no promotion mapped, for every promoted component on this platform (e.g. sx, style, modifier). A name only — what is placed in it is the generator's decision. Absence means unmapped styling is dropped. (ADR-076)

defaultFillWidth.description: Width in pixels of the container this platform places a component in when the component's root resizes to fill its parent. Applies only when the root's layoutSizingHorizontal is FILL; fixed and hugging roots are unaffected. Absence means the platform declares no width and the rendering tool uses its own fallback. (ADR-081)

GlyphStructure.description: Structural form of the glyphs convention (ADR-103): membership from child structure, naming from the component name. A component is a glyph when every child matches some entry in children (set-cover, exhaustive); when fill is declared, every matched leaf must carry one of the listed fills.

name.description: Naming rule applied to the component name, using the {i} placeholder. Defaults to '{i}' — the whole component name is the glyph name.

fill.description: Accepted leaf fills: a raw color ('#RRGGBB') or a token/variable/style name. Tested only on a component's stored structure — an instance mirror is contextually recolored, so fill is skipped there. Absence means fills are not tested.

children.description: Node matchers covering the component's children.

GlyphStructureNode.description: One node matcher within a GlyphStructure. type is an open string carrying a Figma node type (e.g. 'VECTOR', 'BOOLEAN_OPERATION'); an unknown type never matches.

type.description: Figma node type this entry matches.

name.description: Layer name, literal with '*' wildcard. Absence means any name.

children.description: Matchers covering this node's own children, same set-cover semantics. Absence means children are not tested.

Conventions.description: Facts about the libraries a spec was generated from and is generated for, keyed by platform. Figma is one key among react, web-components, swiftui — keys name implementations, not platform families. Absence of platforms means nothing is declared. (ADR-073)

platforms.description: Platform-keyed conventions. The key is a free-form implementation id (figma, react, swiftui).

primitives.description: Component-keyed promotion entries, keyed by the design system's own component name. Platform-neutral and deliberately not under platforms: a component's props are the same whichever platform renders it. Absence means nothing is promoted. (ADR-075)

specs.description: Conventions about the spec itself, loaded from conventions/specs.yaml.

storybook.description: Workspace Storybook conventions — how its pages present, and where it serves. Loaded from conventions/storybook.yaml — a reserved basename, not a platform.

MetadataConventions.description: The conventions a spec records in its metadata: the one platform entry that produced it, and the spec conventions it was produced under. A subset of Conventions reusing the same definitions, so an entry validates identically wherever it appears — but absence means something different. Here a missing platform did not produce this spec. primitives and storybook are deliberately absent: the promotion table is spent by the time a spec exists, and Storybook presentation bears on no reader of one. (ADR-079, ADR-099)

platforms.description: Exactly one entry: the platform this spec was produced from.

specs.description: Conventions about the spec itself, as the producing run resolved them. Optional, unlike platforms: a run that declared none records none. Required by a consumer that has to recover a spec convention it cannot re-derive from the spec — slots.default is the case, since a render resolving a nested instance's default slot does not hold that instance's own component spec.

PrimitiveRule.description: One rule turning something a captured layer carries into props on the component it promotes to. `source` names what is read — a Styles member, a dotted path into typography, or content. The honoured set is closed per PrimitiveKind and documented rather than enumerated here, so the validation surface does not track the Styles key set. Exactly one of prop and values is given. (ADR-075)

source.description: What is read from the captured layer — a Styles member, a dotted path into typography (e.g. typography.fontStyle), or content.

prop.description: The prop this source's value is written to, as-is.

values.description: Literal lookup from what the source carries to the props it writes. A key is a full token path or a raw scalar, never a fragment and never matched partially. One key may write several props, and may write a prop whose meaning differs from the source's.

PrimitiveEntry.description: One component a captured primitive layer can be promoted to, and how its styles become that component's props. Promotion runs during capture, over composed example content only. Several entries may share a kind; a declared match selects by name and takes precedence, and otherwise selection is by how many rules resolve, where at least one must. (ADR-074, ADR-075, ADR-100)

elementType.description: The anatomy element type this component can be promoted from. Named for ElementType, the superset it draws from.

match.description: Layer-name prefixes selecting this entry, within the entries whose elementType matches. A name matches when the captured layer's name starts with one of these strings — exact, case-sensitive, no normalisation, and nothing read out of the name. A resolved match selects the entry immediately: no score is computed and no rule in map need resolve. Where several entries match, the longest matching prefix wins, so selection never depends on authored key order. Absence means this entry is selected by score. (ADR-100)

map.description: Rules turning the layer's styles into this component's props, in precedence order. When two rules write the same prop, the first that resolves wins. May be empty for an entry selected by match whose every prop is a default.

PrimitiveKind.description: The spec element types that can be promoted to a design system component — a strict subset of ElementType. An image is deliberately absent: it is a paint on an element that is already something else, so it is bound through images.component. (ADR-074)

PropReference.description: A prop named by a convention. An object rather than a bare name so it can grow properties of its own without a breaking change.

SpecsConventions.description: Conventions about the spec itself rather than about any platform. A sibling of `platforms` for the same reason `primitives` is: `states` names a prop and an enum value that exist in api.yaml, and a transform reading only the spec can apply it. Library-wide; the per-component equivalent is an annotation, and the annotation wins.

slots.description: Slot-related naming conventions. Absence means no such convention. A spec convention rather than a platform one: what is named is a SlotProp the spec declares, so every platform reads the same answer. (ADR-099)

default.description: The component's designated default slot — the one slot always composed through. Absence means no default-slot convention.

match.description: Naming patterns identifying a component's designated default slot — the SlotProp further content is always composed through. A library may name this slot differently across component families (e.g. children in one, items in another); any pattern in the array matches. When a slot prop matches, specs-from-figma records defaultSlot: true on that SlotProp in the generated spec, and a filling instance may then be nested as a plain child element rather than through an explicit slot binding. Absence means no default slot is designated and every slot binds explicitly.

states.description: Concept-keyed map classifying Figma variant props as semantic states.

accessibility.description: Props carrying accessibility semantics no element expresses.

label.description: The prop supplying an accessible name for a control with no text of its own. A resolving `label` part role wins over it.

value.description: The prop supplying a control's value where no element represents it. A resolving `value` part role wins over it.

ValueConvention.description: The props describing a control's value. `indeterminate` sits here rather than among the state concepts: those are a governed vocabulary where `indeterminate` means a checkbox's mixed state, and a progress bar with no known value is a different fact wearing the same word.

indeterminate.description: A boolean prop that forces the indeterminate presentation regardless of the value.

StorybookConventions.description: Workspace Storybook conventions, keyed by concern, each holding per-feature settings. Most concerns are publish concerns naming how a page presents; `host` names where the Storybook serves. Both levels are open (ADR-098): feature vocabulary is validated by the concern implementation, which warns by name on anything unknown.

additionalProperties.description: One concern's feature settings. Values are deliberately unconstrained here.
